answers.question: I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?
answers.answer:
Not quite yet, and here is the honest version. You raced a marathon 14 days ago; the common rule of thumb is roughly one easy day per mile raced before full training resumes, so about three more weeks before real intensity. Jumping from 12 mi to 40 mi in one week is a 28 mi swing, which is where most post-marathon niggles start.

What I would rather do: climb to about 23 mi next week, 30 mi the week after, then 36–40 mi with the first light faster work (strides and short tempo) in two weeks. If the Thanksgiving 10K matters, we can shape a 3-week sharpening block into it; if it is a fun run, we keep base-building. Tell me which one and I will build it in.

new.analysis:
## How the week landed

You executed the recovery plan cleanly: three easy runs at 3, 4 and 5 mi, pain 0/10 throughout, and the Sunday run came in at 9:51/mi at 139 bpm, which is right on your pre-race easy numbers. That is a healthy bounce-back two weeks out from the race.

## Why I am still holding the reins

The thing a marathon costs you is not visible on a watch for about three weeks: muscle fibers, connective tissue and immune system are still rebuilding even when the legs feel fine. The classic pattern is that athletes feel bulletproof around day 10–14, pile on volume and intensity, and pick up a calf or Achilles problem in week four. I would rather spend one more conservative week and have you training hard and healthy in November than chase the "itching to train" feeling now.

## What next week does

It adds a bit of volume (about 23 mi), returns to your normal five-day pattern, and introduces four short strides on Wednesday to wake up turnover without any real intensity cost. Sunday nudges the long run back toward 7 mi, still fully conversational. If this lands well, next week we go to roughly 30 mi and add a few more strides, and the week after we can bring back a short tempo or a goal-specific session.

## I need direction from you

Two open questions drive the next month: do you want to actually race the Thanksgiving 10K (sharpen for it) or just run it with your friend, and what is the next real goal after that — spring marathon, something shorter, or a base block? Answer those and I will shape November around them.
